graph_requirements: one static axis is fully partitioned by Split or complete sibling Slice routes
all Slice bounds and steps are immutable and equivalent to the Split sizes
output order, shape, dtype, names, and consumers can be preserved

observation: Equivalent static channel-routing representations can lower differently on QNN NPU.
mechanism: Split and sibling Slice can lower differently and can expose different downstream matcher structure; neither representation is intrinsically faster.

directions: static Split -> complete static Slice siblings
complete static Slice siblings -> static Split

expected_evidence.graph: Exact router replacement with unchanged public outputs
expected_evidence.trace: Changed routing operators with no unexplained layout or partition regression

outcome.finding: Either direction can win depending on the surrounding graph and toolchain.
outcome.interaction: A representation-only effect may be small while its downstream matcher-enabling effect is material.
outcome.decision: Treat both directions as scoped paired candidates rather than a universal preference.

counterexamples: The opposite direction was confirmed on another graph revision; do not promote either representation globally.

provenance.scope_note: exact model, graph occurrence, toolchain, artifacts, and measurements remain run-local

discovery.lesson: Split and Slice are competing scoped representations; measure both directions.
